issues.failure_explanation: Axiom (A6) requires, for every delta in [delta_th, delta_bar), that equality in (A5) holds iff grad R = 0. The scalar remainder carries the factor (delta - eta), so at delta = eta it vanishes identically. Hence I(eta; GD(x)) = 0 for every boundary point, stationary or not. (A6) therefore fails at delta = eta, and the remark's claim that all axioms hold with delta_th = eta (closed endpoint) is wrong. The same closed-endpoint convention reappears in the statement of the state-parameter range delta_t in [eta, 2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the threshold as an open endpoint (A5/A6 on (eta, delta_bar)), or require (A6) only for delta > delta_th. The proofs already use delta in (eta, 2).
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the scalar certificate is an instance of the axiomatic framework with threshold eta is false as written at the endpoint delta = eta. Strictness of the monotone state parameter at that endpoint is also unsupported.
issues.title: Axiom check for the scalar certificate fails at the claimed threshold delta_th = eta
issues.why_classification: A local change of the endpoint convention fixes the claim, and no result or conclusion is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof determines P only on level sets that contain an unbalanced stationary point x_* of the loss. Axioms (A1)-(A7) never require that each level set {I(delta; x)=0} contain a global minimizer, and (A5)/(A6) are only assumed for delta >= delta_th(eta). Moreover, delta is an abstract index of the family, but the proof sets delta := 4 a_*^2/(a_*^4+1), which silently fixes the labelling (the family is determined at most up to reparametrisation). The step 'every nonterminal level set compatible with the axioms is forced to coincide' is therefore not a consequence of the axioms. What is proved is only that any level set through an unbalanced minimizer must be the stated ellipse. The theorem's claims of uniqueness 'for every delta in [delta_th, delta_bar)' and of uniqueness of the whole family on (0,2] are unsupported.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing axioms explicitly: each level set for delta >= delta_th contains an unbalanced global minimizer, and the state index is normalised as in the statement. Restate uniqueness up to reparametrisation, for level sets with delta >= delta_th. The existing Lagrange computation then proves the restated result.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim that the scalar certificate is uniquely determined by the structural axioms is overstated. It holds only under extra assumptions (each level set meets the minimizer set, normalised indexing delta in (0,2], threshold range). This also weakens the narrative that the certificates 'arise from the monotonicity structure' rather than from the algebraic construction.
issues.title: Uniqueness theorem relies on unstated assumptions (minimizer on every level set, fixed labelling of delta, range of delta)
issues.why_classification: The computation survives, but the theorem needs new hypotheses and a weakened uniqueness conclusion (up to reparametrisation, for delta >= delta_th). That is more than a local fix, yet a comparable result remains.
